chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the lost one, how should his wife be dealt with? He (peace be upon him) said: If she is silent from it and has been patient, she would be left alone, but if she raises her matter to the ruler, her term is four years. Then he should write to the region in which he disappeared. So let him ask about him, and if there is news of him being alive, she has to be patient, and if there is no news about him, until the four years have passed, he would call the guardian of the lost husband, so he would say to him, ‘Is there wealth for the lost one?’ So if there was wealth for the lost for him, it would be spent upon her until his living from his death would be known.

And if there is no wealth for him, he would say to the guardian, ‘Spend upon her. So if he were to do that, so there is no way for her to be remarried, and if he does not spend upon her, the ruler would compel him that he should divorce with one divorce during the inception of the waiting period and she is pure. Thus a divorce of the guardian would be a divorce of the husband. So if her husband were to come before the fulfillment of her waiting period, from the day the guardian divorced her, so it would be inevitable for him to revert to her, for she is his wife, and she is with him upon the two (remaining) divorces. So if her waiting period has passed before he is (found) alive, or he returns, so she is free for the marriage, and there is no way for the first (husband) upon her’.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal procedure for a wife when her husband goes missing and is presumed dead?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential framework for 'al-mafqud' (the missing person), emphasizing the four-year waiting period established by the Imam to balance legal certainty with compassion. It highlights the role of the Wali (guardian) in managing the missing husband's estate to support his wife, ensuring her financial stability until his status is confirmed as either alive or dead. The text further clarifies the mechanics of proxy divorce and remarriage, reflecting the Shia emphasis on judicial discretion in resolving marital uncertainty.
